PLA-465 plant dimensions: mature_height_ft [10, 20] ft, spread not stated on the page, basis: species (sour orange (Citrus aurantium) is listed among 'Rootstocks used' with no size statement; size effects are given only for rough lemon ('extremely vigorous'), macrophylla ('very vigorous') and Cleopatra mandarin ('slower to come into bearing and fruit size appears smaller'); Swingle citrumelo and Changsha mandarin recommended for acid-to-neutral sandy soils named on the page); UF/IFAS Extension (EDIS), https://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/HS402 (raw read 2026-09-16, 158367 bytes, sha256 50436e71fe8fb2bcaee7949f83f9fb192cdc3c0cbe875f7b6b74808f5f9459fb); verbatim: "The lemon tree is vigorous, upright, and spreading, with an open growth habit (Tucker and Wardowski 1976). Trees may reach 10–20 ft (3.1–6.1 m) in height (Morton 1987).   ||   Rootstock selection for the soil type and conditions is critical. Rootstocks used include rough lemon (C. jambhiri), 'Cleopatra mandarin' (C. reticulata), Volkamer lemon (C. volkameriana), sour orange (C. aurantium) and macrophylla (C. macrophylla) (Tucker and Wardowski 1976). Trees on rough lemon rootstocks are extremely vigorous and susceptible to foot rot (phytophthora). [...] Trees on macrophylla are also very vigorous and susceptible to tristeza [...] Lemons on Cleopatra mandarin are slower to come into bearing and fruit size appears smaller.   ||   (pruning target, not mature size) Trees should be maintained at 7 to 10 ft (2.1–3.1 m) high and 10 to 15 ft (3.1–4.6 m) wide.". Authored from a read the reader marked partial: the page states the species size on a standard, non-dwarfing rootstock, which is the required basis on this crop because its recommended rootstock is a standard stock. amend-not-recert.
